The *Aparauttarattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the meritorious deeds and past-life aspirations of an elder named Uttara, distinguished here by the prefix *apara-* ("another" or "subsequent") to differentiate him from the subject of the immediately preceding *Uttarattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 558) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallels or cross-language alignments with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan texts are registered for this work [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In addition, extensive verse parallels within the Therāpadāna itself include substantial matches with the *Dhātupūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 488, segments 0.3–5.3), as well as thematic and formulaic alignments with the *Upavānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 562), the *Gayākassapattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 555), the *Ekapattadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 504), and the preceding *Uttarattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 558) [DharmaNexus].
